repo_notes.content: This repository packages mruby/c release4.0.0 as a west module for Zephyr v3.7.2 LTS. The unmodified runtime is in vendor/mrubyc/src/. The integration is in zephyr/ and cmake/.
The release4.0.0 archive contains the upstream Zephyr HAL. scripts/check-vendor.sh compares the checked-in HAL and runtime with the same archive.

The module's 4.0.0 runtime requires mrbc 4.0.0 and RITE0400 bytecode. Users upgrading from v3.4.1 must regenerate every embedded script. CI uses Zephyr SDK 0.16.9. The module requires a 32-bit little-endian single-core Zephyr build with multithreading and a system clock.
README.md is the only user-facing document; issues, pull requests, review comments, and code comments are written in English by repository policy.

pages.title: What does this Zephyr module provide?
pages.purpose: Module composition: how west.yml, zephyr/module.yml, vendor/mrubyc, zephyr/, and cmake/ fit together to build mruby/c inside a Zephyr application, plus the platform constraints the Kconfig enforces.

page_notes.content: west.yml pins Zephyr v3.7.2 (clone-depth 1, cmsis name-allowlist) and places the module itself at modules/lib/mrubyc-zephyr, so this repository can also serve as a complete standalone workspace manifest.
zephyr/module.yml declares build.cmake: zephyr and kconfig: zephyr/Kconfig and registers samples/ and tests/ for Twister.
zephyr/Kconfig gates everything on CONFIG_MRUBYC, which requires MULTITHREADING && SYS_CLOCK_EXISTS && !SMP && !BIG_ENDIAN && !64BIT.
The application supplies the memory pool and creates tasks; the module supplies the VM, the Zephyr HAL, and the compile-definition contract shared between them.

pages.title: How do I add the module and run Ruby bytecode?
pages.purpose: Consumption flow: the west manifest entry or EXTRA_ZEPHYR_MODULES, the required prj.conf symbols, bytecode header generation, and the mrbc_init/mrbc_create_task/mrbc_run lifecycle rules.
pages.parent: What does this Zephyr module provide?

page_notes.content: prj.conf needs CONFIG_MRUBYC=y plus CONFIG_PRINTK=y for console output. Select a system clock frequency that represents CONFIG_MRUBYC_TICK_UNIT_MS as a whole number of Zephyr ticks. CMake reports when Zephyr rounds the period up.

Pass an 8-byte-aligned static pool to mrbc_init, then pass each bytecode array to mrbc_create_task and call mrbc_run. With the default CONFIG_MRUBYC_SCHEDULER_EXIT=y, the scheduler returns when no runnable, waiting, or suspended tasks remain.

The VM is single-threaded: access it from one Zephyr thread and let mruby/c schedule Ruby tasks inside it. Keep the pool and bytecode alive for the runtime's lifetime, and use bytecode built from trusted sources.

pages.title: How is Ruby source compiled into the build?
pages.purpose: Describe the mrbc 4.0.0 toolchain, the mrubyc_embed_script helper, and the compiler version and RITE format checks.
pages.parent: What does this Zephyr module provide?

page_notes.content: cmake/mrubyc.cmake's mrubyc_embed_script(target, symbol, source.rb) generates <symbol>.h in the build directory via a custom command that re-runs the same file in CMake script mode. It requires an existing target, CONFIG_MRUBYC=y, a valid unique C identifier per target (tracked in the MRUBYC_EMBEDDED_SYMBOLS property), and an existing .rb file.

The helper verifies the compiler is exactly the MRUBY_VERSION recorded in vendor/mrubyc/src/VERSION, and the script-mode pass checks the generated header actually starts with the RITE version parsed from load.c — output from the wrong compiler fails the build.

mrbc comes from PATH or -DMRUBYC_MRBC=<absolute path>. scripts/build-mrbc.sh builds mruby 4.0.0 from a source archive with a pinned SHA-256. scripts/check-bytecode.sh regenerates every sample header and compares it against the committed copy.

pages.title: Which Kconfig and CMake contracts exist?
pages.purpose: The CONFIG_MRUBYC_* option map, how zephyr/CMakeLists.txt exports it through the MRUBYC_API interface library, alignment handling for ARMv6-M and unaligned traps, and the libm edge case.
pages.parent: What does this Zephyr module provide?

page_notes.content: README.md lists the supported options and upstream restrictions. Options include VM and symbol limits, symbol lookup, Float precision, Math, UTF-8 and Unicode, INT64, NaN boxing, extended operands, destructor callbacks, key-value table sizing, pool profiling, console methods and CRLF, VM diagnostics, exception depth, task names, and scheduler timing and exit.

zephyr/CMakeLists.txt defines the interface library MRUBYC_API carrying include directories and compile definitions; consumers link it with zephyr_library_link_libraries(MRUBYC_API) so application and runtime headers always agree on structure layout.

On ARMv6-M/ARMv8-M baseline or CONFIG_TRAP_UNALIGNED_ACCESS it defines MRBC_REQUIRE_32BIT_ALIGNMENT because RITE bytecode contains halfwords and words at unaligned offsets; TRAP_UNALIGNED_ACCESS also adds -mno-unaligned-access.

USE_MATH adds _DEFAULT_SOURCE to c_math.c (M_E and M_PI are outside C99) and links libm only for native targets that do not already link it (CONFIG_NATIVE_LIBC && !CONFIG_NATIVE_LIBRARY). Single-precision float also demotes -Wdouble-promotion because upstream forwards floats to variadic functions.

pages.title: How does the Zephyr HAL drive the scheduler?
pages.purpose: Describe the periodic k_timer that calls mrbc_tick, nested IRQ and scheduler locking, printk console output, and k_panic abort.
pages.parent: What does this Zephyr module provide?

page_notes.content: mrbc_hal_init starts a periodic Zephyr timer that calls mrbc_tick. When idle, the scheduler sleeps for the configured timer period.

Kconfig preserves the upstream HAL defaults of a 1 ms tick, 10 ticks per time slice, and a return from mrbc_run when active tasks drain. The build passes these values to the HAL and runtime through MRUBYC_API.

IRQ control nests: mrbc_hal_disable_irq pairs irq_lock with k_sched_lock outside ISRs and unwinds on the last enable. mrbc_hal_write emits each byte through printk, and mrbc_hal_abort writes the message then calls k_panic() and k_fatal_halt(K_ERR_KERNEL_PANIC).
hal.h keeps legacy compatibility macros (hal_init, hal_write, hal_abort, ...) mapped to the mrbc_hal_* names used by older mruby/c ports.

pages.title: What do the samples and tests verify?
pages.purpose: samples/hello, samples/vm_tasks, tests/mrubyc (ztest), and tests/posix: what each proves and how Twister scenarios are declared in sample.yaml and testcase.yaml.
pages.parent: What does this Zephyr module provide?

page_notes.content: Samples use Twister's console regex harness on native_sim and qemu_cortex_m3: hello expects 'Hello from mruby/c on Zephyr!' then 'mruby/c finished'; vm_tasks expects the interleaved 'a:start', 'b:ran', 'a:done' then 'Scheduler returned 0'.

tests/mrubyc checks that Kconfig values reach the public headers. The RITE0400 runtime rejects a v3.4.1 RITE0300 fixture, then runs a timed sleep and pattern match. An OP_EXT script runs if and only if extended operands are enabled. The suite also checks task names, exception traces, destructor callbacks, and scheduler idle behavior.
testcase.yaml covers defaults, extended operands disabled, strict alignment on qemu_cortex_m3, custom runtime settings, scheduler idle, NaN boxing, and console and allocator diagnostics.

tests/posix/main.c is compiled by scripts/posix-smoke.sh as a -m32 host binary against the upstream POSIX HAL extracted from the release tarball, asserting the same 'a:start','b:ran','a:done' schedule.

pages.title: How is the vendored upstream kept in sync?
pages.purpose: The integrity scripts: fetch-mrubyc.sh's pinned release and sha256, and check-vendor.sh's verification of the runtime diff, the exclusion list, SRCS parity with the upstream Makefile, and the HAL diff against upstream.
pages.parent: What does this Zephyr module provide?

page_notes.content: scripts/fetch-mrubyc.sh downloads the release4.0.0 tarball and verifies its pinned SHA-256.

check-vendor.sh diffs vendored src/*.c, *.h, VERSION, and the licenses against the release archive. Every other file upstream ships in src/ must appear in a known_exclusions list (Makefile, UnicodeData.txt, hal_selector.mk); a new upstream file fails the check until a reviewer decides to vendor or exclude it.
The same script compares zephyr_library_sources with the upstream src/Makefile SRCS list and diffs zephyr/hal/{hal.c,hal.h,LICENSE} against the HAL in the release4.0.0 archive.
These checks run in CI's 'Bundled source and bytecode' job together with check-bytecode.sh, so drift in the vendored runtime, the HAL, or the committed bytecode headers fails the build.

pages.title: How do CI and releases work?
pages.purpose: ci.yml's Twister, bytecode, POSIX smoke, and workflow-validation jobs, and release.yml's tag validation, environment policy check, and gated GitHub release.
pages.parent: What does this Zephyr module provide?

page_notes.content: ci.yml runs Twister on native_sim (host toolchain, gcc-multilib) and qemu_cortex_m3 (Zephyr toolchain, SDK 0.16.9 installed by scripts/setup-zephyr-sdk.sh with sha256-checked downloads), caching west projects, SDK archives, and ccache.

The composite action .github/actions/setup-mrbc builds and caches mrbc, then verifies it by regenerating the sample bytecode headers via scripts/check-bytecode.sh. A separate 'workflows' job runs actionlint (pinned tarball plus sha256, with .github/actionlint.yaml registering the ubuntu-26.04 label) and shellcheck over scripts/.

release.yml on v* tags first verifies the tag equals the vendored MRUBYC_VERSION and is an ancestor of main, and that the production environment requires reviewers and allows v* tags; it then reuses ci.yml via workflow_call and publishes the GitHub release under the production environment.
